title: ProvFold 0.1.2: provenance-aware direction-based microbiome evidence synthesis
description:
ProvFold is a Python package for provenance-aware synthesis of qualitative microbiome evidence. It links source records to analyst-declared provenance groups and taxonomic mappings, retains the paths to votes and abstentions, and compares counting rules, support thresholds and group omissions. Researchers can use these outputs to audit the sources sustaining a recurrence and reassess evidence maps as source annotations or review questions change.

Version 0.1.2 provides Python and command-line interfaces, source-linked alcohol-associated hepatitis (AH) and hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) examples, and a controlled benchmark of 18 scenarios, 1,720 replicates and 30,960 configured-cell evaluations. Eighteen configurations represent ten distinct estimators. In the HCC example at support 2 and opposition 0, 14 of 16 panel-based selections each drew all their support from a single provenance group: 13 from HCC-F02 and 1 from HCC-F01. Group collapse retained 2 selections. Simulations quantify counting, mapping and threshold behaviour, while separate public-resource analyses assess evaluability.

The source archive contains the package, examples, documentation, recipes and validators. The companion reproducibility archive contains Tables S1–S47 in machine_readable/, synthetic streams, generated analytical results, dated validation records and figures. Its DATA_DICTIONARY.md explains fields and units, DATA_CATALOG.csv inventories the files, and machine_readable/TABLE_MAP.csv links formal tables to source and generation entries. The qualitative AH workflow and its quantitative alpha-diversity companion share a source registry but have different estimands.

Core execution requires Python 3.11 or later and no third-party runtime dependencies. Building from source requires setuptools >=68. Public-resource reconstruction requires openpyxl 3.1.5 and five separately obtained inputs with matching SHA-256 identities. Plotting requires Matplotlib, NumPy and Pillow. The database input acquisition date is 13 August 2026; it is not a software execution or literature-search date.

Interpretation depends on the declared sources and mappings. Publication or BioProject identifiers do not establish participant independence, and ProvFold does not discover cohorts, infer missing taxonomic lineage or validate clinical utility. The AH review reports aggregate full-text exclusion categories; the citation-level list and individual reasons for 161 exclusions were not recorded.

Software is licensed under MIT. Author-produced reproduction inputs and derived tables are CC BY 4.0. Third-party exports and row-level database reconstructions are excluded and retain their own rights. Each distribution includes a file-level SHA-256 inventory; retain the source revision or archive checksum when reporting a run.
